Messages.Author: Teeka
Messages.Body:
I was wondering, are the contents of a tournament pack (or kit?)
always the same, or are they randomly sorted like boosters, or are
there perhaps different versions available?
I was wondering because I found info on a pack containing "old"
promos, and a pack containing nothing more than a non-legal storyline
deck and 5 copies of the same (legal) promo, but I'm not sure if they
were the same "thing" though.

Is the only way to get these packs through attending tournaments, or
can they be ordered/bought as well? As far as I know, no promo has
ever been reprinted in an expansion, right?
The main reason I ask this, is because me and my friends are not very
keen on competitive play, but we'd love to own some of the promo cards
without having to resort to eBay and such.

Thanks,

Teeka

Messages.Author: The Lasombra
Messages.Body:
On 3 Apr 2007 13:45:52 -0700, "Teeka" <teeka_...@hotmail.com>
wrote:

>I was wondering, are the contents of a tournament pack (or kit?)
>always the same, or are they randomly sorted like boosters, or are
>there perhaps different versions available?

Depending on when they were packaged and sent to the distributor,
there have been a variety of tournament kits, that sell for $12 each.
The current kits contain 12 of each of the following cards:

Botched Move
Call the Wild Hunt
Crematorium
Ensemble
Angelo
Victor Pelletier (or Kisha Bhimji)
Blood Doll
Wake with Evening's Freshness

and three random sealed booster packs.

>I was wondering because I found info on a pack containing "old"
>promos, and a pack containing nothing more than a non-legal storyline
>deck and 5 copies of the same (legal) promo, but I'm not sure if they
>were the same "thing" though.

No, they are different articles.
The deck you found was the Millenium Cultist Storyline Kit. It sells
thru White Wolf's website and no tournament need be run to acquire it.
It is 7.49.
http://secure1.white-wolf.com/catalog/product_info.php?products_id=849

>Is the only way to get these packs through attending tournaments, or
>can they be ordered/bought as well?

The Millenium Cultist Storyline Kit can be purchased without running a
tournament or attending one.

>As far as I know, no promo has ever been reprinted in an expansion, right?

To this point, only promotional vampires have been reprinted in sets.
See also:

Lucita
Fatima
Kestrelle Hayes

Promotional library cards have not been reprinted in a booster or a
starter.

>The main reason I ask this, is because me and my friends are not very
>keen on competitive play, but we'd love to own some of the promo cards
>without having to resort to eBay and such.

Run a local event, a multi-deck, multi-judge affair or a storyline
event, when the next one comes around and pick up some tournament
support then.

If you buy your cards from a store, they may also be willing to order
a tournament kit for you without requiring that a tournament be run.
It has been known to happen in the past.

Carpe noctem.

Lasombra

http://www.TheLasombra.com/whatsnew.htm

Your best online source for information about V:TES.
Now also featuring individual card sales and sales
of booster and starter box displays.

Messages.Author: Teeka
Messages.Body:
On 5 apr, 15:48, "Bram Vink" <jja.v...@hccnet.nl> wrote:
> Why aren't you fond of tournaments?

Bad experiences.

While playing MtG, we came across too many people who weren't that fun
or comfortable to be around. And not just at tourneys, at game fairs
and stores as well.
We found (at least in the places we visited, of course I can't
generalize the whole of the card gaming populus) the stereotype of
"socially inept game-geek" to be true far too often. Kinda like what
was said in that other thread about etiquette: lots of verbal
fighting, impatience with people less familiar with the game,
shouting, people giving others the impression to be looking down on
them by verbal and physical expressions, etc (not too mention some
people's BO.. gasp.).

Me and my friends are all people who try to win, but never at the
expense of having a good time. Meaning, we don't do any psychological
warfare, we help others out for sake of keeping the game going (for
instance when we see that their game might crumble because of a small
oversight), and we deliberately play decks that are not killer-good,
but as good as they get while still in the grey area of "fun to play
with and against", if you get what I mean.
Practically everyone we met back then, played strictly to win through
whatever means though, which in MtG terms (of a couple of years back,
mind) meant mono-red, blue-white lock, decks packed with 30-dollars-a-
piece-power-rares etc. We were never any match for those decks and
frankly, people expressed frequence annoyance with us for wasting
their time playing less than killer decks, while at the same time we
saw no fun in playing against the same decks over and over (and
getting a frown and a "tsk" to boot).

Another thing was, some of us are female, which was apparently enough
reason for lots of guys to act like total idiots and not give people
enough personal space, if you get my meaning.

So after a while, we decided to just play socially amongst ourselves.

Also, when some of us first started learning VTES some years back, we
again only played with people who were not able and/or willing to
relate to new players and just kicked our asses from the word go
instead of trying to help us.
This put us off this game entirely, and if it hadn't been for my
personal addiction to games with expansion sets and the fact that
MtG's change of lay-out and constant rules-changes put us off buying
new cards for that game after the Invasion set, we might not have been
playing VTES at all now.

So, yeah I reckon lots of people out there are cool and we just never
met them, but because of our experiences we just got into this
attitude where we just want to play amongst ourselves and have fun. I
guess in our case, the proverbial rotten apples ruined it for the
rest.

What better opportunity to meet
> some other players and get some new ideas about the game? ;)

That's why I frequent this forum! I'm learning lots of things from all
of you and passing that knowledge on..

> I think your perception of what tournaments are like is a a bit
> skewed :)
>

Very likely. It's just hard to shake off bad experiences sometimes.

> I'm sure you'd have a perfectly fun day, at the very least.
>

When we get comfortable enough with the rules and flow of the game, we
might try and leave our secluded cave behind the waterfall to see if
we can find another group of people who we feel comfortable around.
We'll see.

Yeah, in VTES tournaments, the "socially inept geek" is usually the
rarity, as social skills help so tremendously much with successful VTES
play. Still, there are the few exceptions... You shouldn't let that
hinder your group from participation in the wider VTES scene. By and
large, they're an incredibly decent and friendly community of people.

That said, you know there's nothing keeping you from running a non-
sanctioned tournament to your own goals and standards, for your own
group. In the past I've done plenty of "odd" things, like offering
prizes for sportsmanship, prizes for last place (they need more
resources!!), etc. You don't need to be a Prince, and you don't need to
be running a sanctioned event to buy, and use, a tourney pack.
